projects.title: Build: Responsive Landing Page
projects.description:
Pixel-perfect implementation of a Figma or Dribbble design.

THE PROBLEM
A brand or individual needs a landing page that presents an offer clearly and works on any device.

WHO IT IS FOR
Visitors arriving from ads or social media on phones.

OBJECTIVE
Implement a given design as a responsive, accessible landing page.

PREREQUISITES
• The lessons and practice in this stage
• Any tools the stage introduced

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Hero with headline and call to action
• A feature/benefits section
• A contact or signup form
• Responsive navigation

CONSTRAINTS
• Semantic HTML
• No CSS framework required unless already learned
• Must work without horizontal scroll at 375px

MILESTONES
• Structure the HTML
• Implement the layout
• Add responsive breakpoints
• Polish spacing and type

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

• All interactive elements are keyboard reachable
• Images have alt text
• No horizontal scroll

• Copying a tutorial without understanding it, so it breaks on any change

• No documentation, so the work cannot be reproduced

Add a subtle entrance animation and a dark-mode variant.

projects.title: Build: Production Deployment & Observability
projects.description:
Take a full-stack app to production: environment configuration, build, CI/CD deploy, health checks, structured logging, and a rollback plan.

THE PROBLEM
A working full-stack app exists locally but has never been deployed reliably or observed in production.

WHO IT IS FOR
A small team that needs repeatable releases without downtime surprises.

OBJECTIVE
Deploy the app to a hosted environment with configuration, CI/CD, health checks, logs, and a rollback plan.

PREREQUISITES
• A complete full-stack app
• A container or build step
• A CI runner (e.g. GitHub Actions)

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Environment-specific configuration via environment variables
• A repeatable build and deploy pipeline
• A health/readiness endpoint
• Structured logs and a basic error-alerting plan

CONSTRAINTS
• No secrets in the repository or image
• Deployment must be reproducible from scratch
• Must not require manual file edits on the server

MILESTONES
• Containerise/build
• Configure environments
• Automate deploy in CI
• Add health checks and logs
• Document rollback

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• A push to main deploys automatically and succeeds
• The app starts from a clean environment with only documented configuration
• A health check reports status
• Rollback steps are documented and tested once

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• Repository with the pipeline config
• A link to the running deployment
• A short operations note (logs, alerts, rollback)

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Hard-coded secrets
• A deploy that only works on one machine
• No way to tell whether the app is healthy

STRETCH GOAL
Add zero-downtime deploys and a staging environment.

projects.title: Build: Deep Learning Transfer Learning Pipeline
projects.description:
Fine-tune a pretrained image model on a small dataset: data augmentation, a train/validation split, tracked experiments, and error analysis on the confusion matrix.

THE PROBLEM
A small labelled image dataset needs a strong model quickly, without training a network from scratch.

WHO IT IS FOR
A team that needs to prove a computer-vision idea works before investing in more data.

OBJECTIVE
Fine-tune a pretrained model and analyse where it fails.

PREREQUISITES
• Python and PyTorch or TensorFlow basics
• A labelled image dataset (can be a small public one)

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Load and split the dataset (train/validation)
• Fine-tune a pretrained model
• Track at least two experiments (e.g. learning rate or augmentation)
• Report a confusion matrix and per-class performance

CONSTRAINTS
• Use a pretrained backbone rather than training from scratch
• Document the split and preprocessing
• Do not leak validation data into training

MILESTONES
• Prepare data
• Baseline run
• Tune/augment
• Evaluate and analyse errors

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The model beats a majority-class baseline on validation
• Experiments are comparable and logged
• At least three concrete error cases are explained

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• Notebook or repository
• Training/validation metrics
• Error-analysis notes with example failures

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Data leakage between splits
• Reporting only accuracy on an imbalanced set
• No baseline to compare against

STRETCH GOAL
Add class weighting and compare against a second backbone.

projects.title: Build: Kubernetes Orchestration & Autoscaling
projects.description:
Deploy a containerised service to a Kubernetes cluster with deployments, services, ingress, config/secrets, resource limits, and a horizontal pod autoscaler validated under load.

THE PROBLEM
A container runs on one host but the app must survive restarts, traffic spikes, and configuration changes.

WHO IT IS FOR
An engineering team standardising deployments on Kubernetes.

OBJECTIVE
Deploy the service to Kubernetes with proper configuration, scaling, and health management.

PREREQUISITES
• Docker fundamentals
• Access to a test cluster (local or cloud)

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Deployment and Service manifests (or Helm chart)
• ConfigMaps/Secrets separation
• Liveness and readiness probes
• Resource requests/limits
• Horizontal Pod Autoscaler validated under load

CONSTRAINTS
• No secrets baked into images
• Workload must be reachable only through the intended ingress
• Must be reproducible from manifests

MILESTONES
• Container image
• Manifests
• Config and probes
• Autoscaling
• Load validation

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Pods recover automatically after being killed
• The HPA scales under synthetic load and scales back down
• Only the ingress exposes the service

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• Manifests/chart in a repository
• Output of `kubectl get`/`describe` for the workload and HPA
• A short load-test summary

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• No resource limits, so one pod starves the node
• Missing readiness probe causing traffic to fail fast
• Secrets committed in plaintext

STRETCH GOAL
Add a rolling-update strategy with zero-downtime verification.

projects.title: Build: Channel Strategy Blueprint
projects.description:
Define a niche, audience, value proposition, and content pillars with evidence of demand. Produce a 90-day publishing plan and success metrics.

THE PROBLEM
A new channel has no clear audience or reason to exist beyond "I want to post videos".

WHO IT IS FOR
The channel creator starting from zero.

OBJECTIVE
Produce a defensible channel strategy before producing content.

PREREQUISITES
• None

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• A specific niche and target viewer
• A value proposition and 3–4 sustainable content pillars
• Evidence of search/audience demand
• A 90-day publishing plan and success metrics

CONSTRAINTS
• Strategy must be affordable to sustain
• Pillars must be realistically producible

MILESTONES
• Audience definition
• Demand research
• Pillars
• 90-day plan

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The niche is specific enough to name the viewer
• Each pillar is justified by demand evidence
• The plan is achievable at the stated cadence

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• A strategy document
• Screenshots of demand research (search/analytics)
• A calendar of the first 12 planned videos

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• A niche so broad it competes with everyone
• Pillars with no evidence of demand
• A cadence the creator cannot sustain

STRETCH GOAL
Add a differentiation analysis against three established channels.

• Using sensitive data in an unapproved tool

projects.title: Build: Clarity Rewrite Clinic
projects.description:
Take a dense, jargon-heavy source (internal doc, release note, or spec) and rewrite it for a defined audience: cut ambiguity, add structure, and justify each change.

THE PROBLEM
A dense internal document is hard for its real audience to act on.

WHO IT IS FOR
A named, non-expert reader who must act on the content.

OBJECTIVE
Rewrite the source for clarity without losing accuracy.

PREREQUISITES
• None

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• A defined audience and purpose
• A restructured version (headings, short paragraphs, examples)
• Annotated justifications for the major changes
• A before/after comparison

CONSTRAINTS
• Do not change technical meaning
• Keep all required information
• Prefer plain language over jargon where possible

MILESTONES
• Audience analysis
• Draft rewrite
• Annotate changes
• Peer check for accuracy

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• A reader can find the key action quickly
• No factual meaning changed
• At least five changes are justified

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• Before and after documents
• An annotated list of changes and why
• A short accuracy review note

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Simplifying until the content is wrong
• No audience definition
• Changes made with no rationale

STRETCH GOAL
Rewrite the same source for a second, more technical audience and compare.

projects.title: Build: Block Explorer Investigation
projects.description:
Trace a real transaction end to end on a testnet explorer: from, to, value, gas, logs, and contract interaction. Explain each field and what the receipt proves.

THE PROBLEM
Beginners trust a transaction hash without understanding what it proves.

WHO IT IS FOR
The learner building on-chain literacy.

OBJECTIVE
Trace and explain a real transaction on a testnet explorer.

PREREQUISITES
• A testnet wallet with a little test ETH

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• A real transaction hash and its receipt
• An explanation of from/to/value/gas/status/logs
• At least one contract interaction with an event log

CONSTRAINTS
• Use a testnet
• Do not expose private keys

MILESTONES
• Make a transaction
• Read the receipt
• Explain each field
• Document the contract call

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

• The log is decoded and interpreted
• The write-up would let a newcomer repeat it

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• A written investigation
• Explorer screenshots or links
• The decoded event log

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Confusing gas used with gas price
• Ignoring the status/logs
• Exposing a key in a screenshot

STRETCH GOAL
Trace the same transaction through a second explorer and reconcile any differences.

projects.title: Build: Self-Custody Wallet Security Setup
projects.description:
Set up and document a self-custody wallet: key/seed handling, hardware or secure storage plan, backup and recovery procedure, and a phishing/approval-risk checklist.

THE PROBLEM
Poor key handling is the most common way people lose funds.

WHO IT IS FOR
The learner securing their own assets.

OBJECTIVE
Set up self-custody with a tested recovery procedure and a risk checklist.

PREREQUISITES
• Wallet and key concepts from this stage

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• A self-custody wallet set up on a testnet or with a hardware wallet
• A documented, offline seed backup plan
• A tested recovery procedure
• A phishing/token-approval risk checklist

CONSTRAINTS
• Never store a real seed phrase digitally in the submission
• Use placeholders in any shared evidence

MILESTONES
• Set up wallet
• Backup plan
• Test recovery
• Write the risk checklist

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Recovery was actually tested
• No real seed is exposed in the submitted evidence
• Checklist covers approvals and phishing

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• A procedure document (with redacted/placeholder secrets)
• A recovery test log
• The risk checklist

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Storing a seed in a screenshot or note app
• Never testing recovery
• Ignoring token approvals

STRETCH GOAL
Add a multisig or social-recovery plan for higher-value holdings.

projects.title: Build: Automated Audit Pipeline
projects.description:
Build a repeatable smart-contract audit pipeline: Slither static analysis, Foundry fuzz/invariant tests, a triage of findings, and a short report distinguishing true positives from noise.

THE PROBLEM
Manual review alone is slow and misses classes of bugs that tools catch quickly.

WHO IT IS FOR
A security-focused developer or auditor.

OBJECTIVE
Build a repeatable, automated-plus-manual audit pipeline.

PREREQUISITES
• Foundry
• The vulnerabilities and auditing lessons in this track

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Slither (or equivalent) static analysis run and triaged
• Foundry fuzz/invariant tests targeting suspected issues
• A triage that separates true positives from noise
• A short findings report

CONSTRAINTS
• Authorized targets only
• Do not report tool output as confirmed findings without validation

MILESTONES
• Run static analysis
• Write fuzz tests
• Validate and triage
• Report

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Each reported finding is validated or clearly marked unconfirmed
• The pipeline is re-runnable
• False positives are explained

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• Pipeline scripts/config
• Tool output
• The triaged report

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Dumping raw tool output as findings
• No validation step
• Missing the false-positive explanation

STRETCH GOAL
Add a CI job that fails on new high-severity findings.

projects.title: Build: Agile vs Waterfall Decision Brief
projects.description:
For two contrasting projects, compare Agile and predictive delivery across uncertainty, scope stability, and regulatory need, then justify a method choice with evidence.

THE PROBLEM
Teams often default to one delivery method without weighing the project's real conditions.

WHO IT IS FOR
A project sponsor deciding how to run a project.

OBJECTIVE
Compare Agile and predictive (waterfall) delivery and justify a choice.

PREREQUISITES
• The Agile and predictive lessons in this track

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Two contrasting project scenarios
• A comparison across uncertainty, scope stability, regulation, and stakeholder access
• A justified recommendation per scenario

CONSTRAINTS
• Base the comparison on the project conditions, not preference
• Cite the factors explicitly

MILESTONES
• Define scenarios
• Compare factors
• Recommend and justify
• Note trade-offs

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Each recommendation follows from the stated conditions
• Trade-offs and risks of the chosen method are acknowledged
• Both scenarios name the specific factors (uncertainty, scope stability, regulation, stakeholder access) that drove the choice

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• A decision brief for both scenarios
• A comparison matrix
• A short risk note per choice

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Choosing a method by fashion
• Ignoring regulatory or contractual constraints
• No acknowledgement of the method's weaknesses

STRETCH GOAL
Add a hybrid approach and explain when it is justified.

projects.title: Build: Experiment Design & Readout
projects.description:
Design a controlled experiment for a product hypothesis: metric, guardrails, sample, success threshold, then write a readout with a ship/iterate/stop recommendation.

THE PROBLEM
A product change is shipped on opinion rather than evidence.

WHO IT IS FOR
A product team deciding whether to invest in a change.

OBJECTIVE
Design a controlled experiment and commit to a pre-registered decision rule.

PREREQUISITES
• The experimentation lessons in this track

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• A falsifiable hypothesis
• A primary metric, guardrail metrics, and a success threshold
• Sample/segment plan and duration
• A pre-committed decision rule (ship/iterate/stop)

CONSTRAINTS
• Decision rule must be set before results
• Guardrails must be able to block a launch

MILESTONES
• Hypothesis
• Metric and threshold
• Design and sample
• Readout template

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The hypothesis is testable and specific
• The success threshold is justified
• The readout applies the rule to realistic results

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• An experiment design document
• A readout using (real or realistic) results
• The final recommendation

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Moving the goalposts after results
• Ignoring a guardrail regression
• Stopping early on a fluke

STRETCH GOAL
Add a second variant and a documented multiple-comparison caveat.

projects.description:
Take one feature from spec to launch: engineering-ready requirements, trade-off notes, launch checklist, rollout plan, and a retrospective on what changed after feedback.

THE PROBLEM
Features slip between a good spec and a working launch.

WHO IT IS FOR
A product team and an engineering partner.

OBJECTIVE
Take one feature from spec to launch and reflect on the outcome.

PREREQUISITES
• The requirements and shipping lessons in this track

FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Engineering-ready requirements with acceptance criteria
• Trade-off notes (scope, quality, time)
• A launch/rollout plan with metrics to watch
• A retrospective on what changed after feedback

CONSTRAINTS
• Requirements must be testable
• Must include a rollback/kill-switch plan

MILESTONES
• Write the spec
• Agree trade-offs
• Plan the rollout
• Reflect on the outcome

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Acceptance criteria are objectively checkable
• The rollout plan states success and failure signals
• The retrospective is candid about what changed

EVIDENCE TO SUBMIT
• The spec
• The rollout plan
• The retrospective

COMMON FAILURE CASES
• Acceptance criteria no one can test
• No rollout safety net
• A retrospective that hides problems

STRETCH GOAL
Add a phased rollout with a feature flag and staged percentages.

Review an authorized contract and report real, reproducible findings.

• An honest list of what was not checked

projects.title: Build: AI Workflow Case Study
projects.description:
Choose one recurring task. Document the original process, identify where AI helps, build the workflow, test three iterations, record failures, define review criteria, and present the before/after process.

BUILD OBJECTIVE
Turn a useful AI technique into a repeatable workflow with defined inputs, review gates, and quality criteria.

PREREQUISITE TRACE
• Stage 6: Design a repeatable AI workflow
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 4: Use AI selectively while retaining human judgment
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 5: Verify AI output
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify

DELIVERABLES
• Document the original task, inputs, time cost, and quality problems.
• Define where AI adds value and where human judgment remains required.
• Create reusable instructions, a context template, output format, and review checklist.
• Run at least three iterations and record what failed and what changed.
• Produce a short before/after comparison of the workflow.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The workflow has a clear trigger, input, AI step, review step, and final output.
• Success criteria are defined before evaluating the workflow.
• At least one failure mode is documented with a mitigation.
• Another person could reproduce the workflow from the documentation.

EVIDENCE
• Final workflow
• Before/after example
• Iteration notes
• Review checklist

STRETCH GOAL
Generalize the workflow into a reusable template for a second related task.

projects.title: Build: YouTube Pilot Series
projects.description:
Produce three related videos for one audience. Document research, differentiation, scripts, production, thumbnails, titles, AI disclosures where required, analytics review, and changes for video four.

BUILD OBJECTIVE
Operate an AI-assisted channel with current platform rules, quality controls, and a repeatable improvement loop.

PREREQUISITE TRACE
• Stage 1: Channel strategy and audience proposition
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 2: Topic research and differentiation
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 3: Research-backed scripting
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 4: Packaging and expectation alignment
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 5: Originality and platform quality
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 6: AI disclosure
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 7: Analytics-driven iteration
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify

DELIVERABLES
• Define one audience and a focused channel proposition.
• Research and select three related video topics.
• Write and fact-check the scripts.
• Produce the three videos with documented AI assistance.
• Create titles, thumbnails, descriptions, and publishing metadata.
• Review early performance and document the change planned for video four.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The three videos have a coherent audience and content promise.
• The opening delivers on the packaging promise.
• Material AI-generated or altered content is disclosed where current policy requires it.
• The workflow does not rely on repetitive mass-produced content with little original value.
• Analytics observations lead to a concrete iteration decision.

EVIDENCE
• Channel brief
• Three scripts
• Three videos
• Packaging assets
• Analytics review

STRETCH GOAL
Run a controlled packaging experiment on a later video and document the observed change.

projects.title: Build: AI Engineering Audit
projects.description:
Review an AI-assisted application for architecture, generated-code quality, tests, security, performance, maintainability, and prioritized remediation.

BUILD OBJECTIVE
Define team-level rules for AI-assisted development, including security, review, maintainability, and acceptable use.

PREREQUISITE TRACE
• Stage 1: Understand and inspect AI-generated code
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 2: Write bounded coding requirements
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 3: Debug from evidence
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 4: Delegate bounded agent work
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 5: Control sensitive changes
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 6: Test AI-generated code
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 7: Run a professional AI-assisted development loop
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 8: Team AI policy and review standards
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify

DELIVERABLES
• Inspect the application architecture and generated-code changes.
• Review correctness, security, tests, maintainability, and scope discipline.
• Identify at least five concrete findings and rank them by severity.
• Reproduce the most important defects where possible.
• Propose or implement prioritized remediation.
• Document what the AI handled well and where human review was essential.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Findings are specific, reproducible, and tied to evidence.
• Security and correctness issues are separated from style preferences.
• The remediation plan is prioritized by risk and impact.
• The learner can explain each important change.

EVIDENCE
• Audit report
• Code diff/review notes
• Test evidence
• Remediation plan

STRETCH GOAL
Create a regression test suite that protects the highest-risk findings from reappearing.

projects.title: Build: Production Automation Design
projects.description:
Design an automation with trigger, data contract, transformations, AI step, validation, human approval, retries, logging, failure handling, and maintenance plan.

BUILD OBJECTIVE
Operate an automation reliably with logs, alerts, bounded retries, recovery, and maintenance planning.

PREREQUISITE TRACE
• Stage 1: Select a safe automation candidate
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 2: Design workflows and failure paths
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 3: Specify API boundaries
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 4: Secure webhook actions
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 5: Place AI inside deterministic controls
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 6: Validate structured data contracts
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 7: Use human approval for consequential actions
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 8: Operate and recover automations
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify

DELIVERABLES
• Define the business process, trigger, inputs, and desired outcome.
• Create an explicit data contract between each workflow step.
• Place AI only where probabilistic interpretation adds value.
• Add validation, human approval, logging, retries, and failure handling.
• Describe maintenance and monitoring requirements.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The workflow has a clear happy path and explicit failure paths.
• External inputs are authenticated and validated where appropriate.
• Consequential actions have an appropriate human control.
• The workflow can be explained and maintained by someone else.

EVIDENCE
• Workflow diagram
• Data contracts
• Failure matrix
• Control points
• Maintenance plan

STRETCH GOAL
Create a replay/recovery strategy for failed runs without duplicating irreversible actions.

projects.title: Build: Bounded Agent System
projects.description:
Build a bounded agent. Document tools, permissions, context, memory, planning, evaluation set, failure modes, human approvals, cost limits, and monitoring. Demonstrate five failure cases.

BUILD OBJECTIVE
Justify agent complexity and coordinate specialized agents only when it creates measurable value.

PREREQUISITE TRACE
• Stage 1: Know when an agent is justified
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 2: Prefer deterministic workflows when appropriate
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 3: Design agent goals and boundaries
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 4: Define tool contracts and permissions
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 5: Control context and memory
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 6: Bound recovery and escalation
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 7: Observe and diagnose agent behavior
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 8: Require human approval for high-impact actions
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 9: Evaluate agent behavior
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify

DELIVERABLES
• Define the agent goal and why an agent is justified over a deterministic workflow.
• Document tools, permissions, context, memory, and action boundaries.
• Build the main workflow with bounded recovery and escalation.
• Create an evaluation set covering normal cases, edge cases, and failures.
• Demonstrate at least five failure cases and the resulting controls.
• Document approval and monitoring decisions.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• Every tool has a clear contract and constrained permission set.
• Irreversible or high-impact actions have human approval.
• Evaluation cases have expected outcomes.
• Failure handling is bounded; the agent cannot retry indefinitely.

EVIDENCE
• Architecture diagram
• Tool contracts
• Evaluation set
• Failure demonstrations
• Monitoring plan

STRETCH GOAL
Compare the agent against a simpler deterministic workflow and quantify whether extra complexity is justified.

projects.title: Build: AI-Assisted Design Case Study
projects.description:
Complete a design problem from research to prototype. Show AI explorations, rejected alternatives, accessibility checks, user feedback, final design, and where human judgment changed the output.

BUILD OBJECTIVE
Reject AI suggestions when they conflict with user needs, evidence, accessibility, ethics, or the design goal.

PREREQUISITE TRACE
• Stage 1: Explore design directions with AI
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 2: Evaluate UI against hierarchy and usability
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 3: Maintain visual consistency
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 4: Check accessibility and responsible visual output
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 5: Use evidence to challenge design assumptions
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 6: Prototype and iterate
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 7: Use design-system patterns
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify
• Stage 8: Exercise final design judgment
  Learn → See → Practice → Verify

DELIVERABLES
• Define the product problem, audience, and evidence behind the design goal.
• Explore multiple AI-assisted directions and record why alternatives were rejected.
• Create a coherent interface or prototype using an appropriate design system.
• Run an accessibility review and user feedback cycle.
• Iterate based on evidence and document where human judgment changed the output.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
• The design is grounded in a user problem rather than visual novelty.
• Accessibility requirements are actively checked.
• AI-generated directions are evaluated against constraints.
• The final case study shows iteration, not just the final screenshot.

EVIDENCE
• Problem statement
• Exploration board
• Rejected alternatives
• Prototype
• Accessibility review
• Iteration notes

STRETCH GOAL
Create a reusable design-system pattern or component derived from the final solution.
